transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I go from feeling like I can work nonstop and take on everything to suddenly having no energy to even show up for my shifts. My manager and my mom were getting really worried about these extreme changes, so I promised them I'd come in and get checked out.
How long do these high-energy and low-energy periods typically last when they occur?

The whole back-and-forth cycle has been going on for about four months now. This heavy, low-energy stretch has been dragging me down for about three months, after that high, unstoppable phase lasted for about a month. It's just been really exhausting.
During that month when you felt unstoppable, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual—like only a few hours—but still felt fully energized?

Yeah, definitely. I would stay up all night sketching business plans or deep-cleaning my apartment at 3 a.m., completely insisting to everyone that I didn't need any rest. I felt like I had this endless engine running inside of me, even if I only got a couple of hours of sleep.
During that month when you felt unstoppable, did you find yourself making impulsive decisions, such as spending a lot of money or taking risks you normally wouldn't?

I didn't really do much reckless spending or take crazy risks during that time. In fact, I was actually focused on trying to save money and pay down my existing credit card debt. Though, I definitely was taking on way too many projects and extra shifts at work.
During that month of high energy, did you feel like your thoughts were racing incredibly fast, or did people notice you were talking much faster than usual?

Yes, definitely—my brain felt so revved up that thoughts were flying by faster than I could catch them, jumping rapidly from paying off credit cards to planning a Europe trip and redesigning the restaurant logo. I was also talking constantly and so fast that people couldn't get a word in, and I actually felt physically uncomfortable if there was any pause in the conversation.
During that month when you felt so high-energy and unstoppable, did this behavior cause any serious problems in your relationships or at work, or did it ever lead to you being hospitalized?

I didn't get hospitalized, but it definitely caused some real problems. I was talking down to my manager like I knew more than him, snapping at coworkers, and being so overwhelming that my friends started pulling away. My mom got really worried about the dramatic changes, and my manager eventually pulled me aside because of my erratic performance.
During this current three-month period of low energy, have you lost interest or pleasure in the things you normally enjoy doing?

Yes, I really have. I used to live for playing Sunday soccer and trying out new recipes after work, but now even the thought of doing those things feels totally pointless. Lately, I mostly just sit around scrolling on my phone because I can't find the drive to do anything else.
Along with losing interest in your hobbies, have you also been feeling persistently sad, down, or hopeless during these past three months?

Yes, it's been a really heavy, low stretch for about three months now. I feel completely drained in this prolonged downturn, to the point where I can barely get myself to work or handle basic tasks around the apartment. It just feels like a constant struggle to do anything.
During this difficult three-month low period, have you had any thoughts of death, hurting yourself, or suicide?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself, suicide, or death during this low period. Even though I'm incredibly drained and struggling to get through the days, I've never felt like I wanted to end my life.
During that month of high energy, did you ever hear or see things that others couldn't, or have beliefs that others felt were highly unrealistic or impossible?

I never saw or heard anything unusual, but I definitely had some highly unrealistic beliefs back then. I was absolutely convinced I could launch a food truck and run my own restaurant chain within a year, and I even acted like I knew more about the business than my manager despite dropping out of college.
During these past three months of feeling low, have you been struggling with feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt about things?
No, I haven't really been dealing with feelings of worthlessness or guilt during this time. I'm just mostly overwhelmed by how completely exhausted and drained of energy I am.
During these past three months of feeling low, have you been completely unable to work or take care of yourself, or are you still managing to get by with great difficulty?

I'm barely scraping by with extreme difficulty, and I've already been written up for no-shows at work and fallen behind on my rent and bills. Even basic things like showering, getting dressed, or deciding what to buy at the grocery store are completely exhausting. It honestly feels like I'm constantly trying to move through thick mud just to get by.
During these past three months of feeling low, have you experienced any significant changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite?

My appetite is all over the place—I either forget to eat all day or suddenly inhale a whole pizza at midnight, and my clothes are starting to hang off me. As for sleep, no matter how long I sleep or lie in bed, I wake up feeling completely wiped out and heavy, as if I haven't rested at all.
Have you or others noticed that you are moving and speaking much slower than usual, or conversely, do you feel so physically agitated that you can't sit still?

Yes, I've definitely experienced both extremes. On my low days, I feel like I'm moving in slow motion and even carrying a food tray at work feels like walking through mud. Other times, I'm so restless that I can't stop pacing, fidgeting, and bouncing my leg like I'm about to jump out of my skin.
During these past three months of feeling low, have you experienced significant trouble concentrating, focusing on tasks, or making decisions?

Yes, my head feels foggy all the time now and I've had a really hard time concentrating or making decisions. At work, customers will tell me their order and I've already forgotten half of it by the time I go to punch it into the screen. Even simple things like deciding what to buy at the store leave me just standing there staring at the shelves.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a current 3-month depressive episode characterized by depressed mood, anhedonia, extreme fatigue, sleep disturbances, appetite/weight loss, psychomotor agitation/retardation, and severe concentration difficulties. The severity of the current episode is severe, as evidenced by profound functional impairment (written up for work no-shows, falling behind on rent, and struggling with basic self-care like showering and dressing). There is a documented history of a 1-month manic/hypomanic episode featuring decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, pressured speech, grandiosity, and increased goal-directed activity. The absence of active delusions or hallucinations during the current depressive state confirms the specifier 'without psychotic symptoms'. Thus, the patient meets the criteria for Bipolar affective disorder, current episode severe depression without psychotic symptoms (F31.4).
